# Tao (Jonas) Chen

> Tao (Jonas) Chen is Provost's Chair Professor in Finance at Nanyang Business School, NTU Singapore. His research covers sustainable finance; FinTech, AI, and finance; and how investors and monitors shape corporate policy.

Provost's Chair Professor in Finance, Nanyang Business School, Nanyang Technological University (NTU), Singapore. Email: jtchen@ntu.edu.sg.

## Publications — Sustainable Finance

How environmental, social and governance forces shape firm behaviour: pollution and environmental policy, social responsibility, tax practices, and the oversight of managers.

- [Ecological integrity of avoided deforestation projects](https://taochen.org/research/ecological-integrity-avoided-deforestation-ncc-2026/) — Kelly Ong, Tao Chen, Zhimin Chen, Carlos T. Pérez-Brito, Yiwen Zeng. Nature Climate Change 16, 2026. DOI 10.1038/s41558-026-02657-2. Finding: Across 133 accredited avoided-deforestation carbon projects, most have mixed, negligible or negative effects on the ecological condition of forests relative to matched control areas.
- [Minimum Wages, State Ownership, and Corporate Environmental Policies](https://taochen.org/research/minimum-wages-state-ownership-jfqa-2025/) — Tao Chen, Xi Xiong, Kunru Zou. Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis 60, 2025. DOI 10.1017/S0022109024000644. Finding: Minimum wage increases lead industrial firms to pollute more and reduce abatement, and state ownership mitigates these effects.
- [Labor unionization and real earnings management: Evidence from labor elections](https://taochen.org/research/labor-unionization-real-earnings-plos-one-2024/) — Vivek Astvansh, Beibei Wang, Tao Chen, Jimmy Chengyuan Qu. PLOS ONE 19, 2024. DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0292889. Finding: Firms whose workers narrowly vote to unionize reduce real earnings management relative to firms where the vote narrowly fails.
- [The social cost of investor distraction: Evidence from institutional cross-blockholding](https://taochen.org/research/social-cost-investor-distraction-plos-one-2023/) — Vivek Astvansh, Tao Chen, Jimmy Chengyuan Qu. PLOS ONE 18, 2023. DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0286336. Finding: Institutional investors who hold blocks in several firms in an industry are distracted, and the social performance of cross-held firms suffers.
- [Bank deregulation and corporate environmental performance](https://taochen.org/research/bank-deregulation-corporate-environmental-wd-2023/) — Shiyi Chen, Tao Chen, Pingyi Lou, Hong Song, Chenyu Wu. World Development 161, 2023. DOI 10.1016/j.worlddev.2022.106106. Finding: Bank branching deregulation in China improved the environmental performance of more exposed firms, through technology upgrading and changes in asset mix.
- [The Unintended Consequence of Land Finance: Evidence from Corporate Tax Avoidance](https://taochen.org/research/unintended-consequence-land-finance-ms-2022/) — Tao Chen, Youchao Tan, Jinghua Wang, Cheng (Colin) Zeng. Management Science 68, 2022. DOI 10.1287/mnsc.2021.4191. Finding: When Chinese local governments lose land-sale revenue, they enforce taxes more strictly and firms in their jurisdiction avoid less tax.
- [Globalization and U.S. Corporate Tax Policies: Evidence from Import Competition](https://taochen.org/research/globalization-us-corporate-tax-ms-2022/) — Tao Chen, Chen Lin, Xiang Shao. Management Science 68, 2022. DOI 10.1287/mnsc.2021.4121. Finding: U.S. manufacturers more exposed to Chinese import competition after China received Permanent Normal Trade Relations increase their tax-reduction activities.
- [Does credit rating conservatism matter for corporate tax avoidance?](https://taochen.org/research/credit-rating-conservatism-matter-af-2021/) — Tao Chen, Sidney Leung, Lingmin Xie. Accounting & Finance 61, 2021. DOI 10.1111/acfi.12773. Finding: More conservative credit ratings, following Dodd–Frank and the US sovereign downgrade, led firms to engage in more tax planning.
- [Institutional shareholders and corporate social responsibility](https://taochen.org/research/institutional-shareholders-corporate-social-jfe-2020/) — Tao Chen, Hui Dong, Chen Lin. Journal of Financial Economics 135, 2020. DOI 10.1016/j.jfineco.2019.06.007. Finding: Higher institutional ownership improves firms’ CSR performance, especially in financially material categories, partly through CSR-related shareholder proposals.
- [Does Information Asymmetry Affect Corporate Tax Aggressiveness?](https://taochen.org/research/information-asymmetry-affect-corporate-jfqa-2017/) — Tao Chen, Chen Lin. Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis 52, 2017. DOI 10.1017/S0022109017000576. Finding: Firms avoid taxes more aggressively after an exogenous loss of analyst coverage, especially where tax-planning capacity is high and outside monitoring is weak.
- [Institutions, board structure, and corporate performance: Evidence from Chinese firms](https://taochen.org/research/institutions-board-structure-corporate-jcf-2015/) — Tao Chen. Journal of Corporate Finance 32, 2015. DOI 10.1016/j.jcorpfin.2014.10.009. Finding: Examines how the institutional environment shapes the relation between board structure and the performance of Chinese listed firms.
- [Do analysts matter for governance? Evidence from natural experiments](https://taochen.org/research/analysts-matter-governance-natural-jfe-2015/) — Tao Chen, Jarrad Harford, Chen Lin. Journal of Financial Economics 115, 2015. DOI 10.1016/j.jfineco.2014.10.002. Finding: After an exogenous loss of analyst coverage, CEOs receive higher excess pay, managers make more value-destroying acquisitions and manage earnings more.

## Publications — FinTech, AI, and Finance

How financial technology and artificial intelligence change access to credit, innovation, and the way consumers respond to technology-driven markets.

- [Cultural Lag, Consumer Literacy, and Coping in AI-Enabled Advertising: A Theoretical Explication and Managerial Solutions](https://taochen.org/research/cultural-lag-consumer-literacy-ja-2026/) — Chen Lou, Xuan Zhou, Elison Ai Ching Lim, Tao Chen, Edson C. Tandoc, Diotima Chattoraj. Journal of Advertising 55, 2026. DOI 10.1080/00913367.2026.2652377. Finding: Consumers often cannot tell AI-enabled ads from traditional ones without disclosure, and beliefs, literacy, public policy and education lag behind the technology.
- [What influences demand for Buy Now, Pay Later credit?](https://taochen.org/research/influences-demand-buy-now-el-2024/) — Tao Chen, Ben R. Marshall, Nhut H. Nguyen, Nuttawat Visaltanachoti. Economics Letters 242, 2024. DOI 10.1016/j.econlet.2024.111857. Finding: In New Zealand, Buy Now, Pay Later demand is higher among single, younger and lower-income borrowers and falls as interest rates rise.
- [Authentically Fake? How Consumers Respond to the Influence of Virtual Influencers](https://taochen.org/research/authentically-fake-consumers-respond-ja-2023/) — Chen Lou, Siu Ting Josie Kiew, Tao Chen, Tze Yen Michelle Lee, Jia En Celine Ong, ZhaoXi Phua. Journal of Advertising 52, 2023. DOI 10.1080/00913367.2022.2149641. Finding: Followers see virtual influencers as “authentically fake”: useful for brand awareness, but weak at driving purchase intention.
- [Finance and Firm Volatility: Evidence from Small Business Lending in China](https://taochen.org/research/finance-firm-volatility-small-ms-2022/) — Tao Chen, Yi Huang, Chen Lin, Zixia Sheng. Management Science 68, 2022. DOI 10.1287/mnsc.2020.3942. Finding: Access to FinTech credit on Alibaba’s platform reduces sales volatility and exit risk for small online businesses.
- [Impact of Competition on Innovations of IT Industry: An Empirical Investigation](https://taochen.org/research/impact-competition-innovations-it-jmis-2021/) — Tao Chen, Hsing Kenneth Cheng, Yong (Jimmy) Jin, Shengli Li, Liangfei Qiu. Journal of Management Information Systems 38, 2021. DOI 10.1080/07421222.2021.1962590. Finding: Greater product market competition, identified through import tariff cuts, increases both the number and the quality of IT firms’ patents.
- [Financial innovation: The bright and the dark sides](https://taochen.org/research/financial-innovation-bright-dark-jbf-2016/) — Thorsten Beck, Tao Chen, Chen Lin, Frank M. Song. Journal of Banking & Finance 72, 2016. DOI 10.1016/j.jbankfin.2016.06.012. Finding: Financial innovation is associated with faster growth in industries that rely on it, but also with greater bank fragility and larger losses during the 2007–08 crisis.

## Publications — Investors, Monitors and Corporate Policy

How analysts, owners, regulators and governments shape corporate investment, risk-taking and firm value.

- [Analyst coverage, executive compensation and corporate risk‐taking: Evidence from property–casualty insurance firms](https://taochen.org/research/analyst-coverage-executive-compensation-jri-2023/) — Tao Chen, Shinichi Kamiya, Pingyi Lou, Andreas Milidonis. Journal of Risk and Insurance 90, 2023. DOI 10.1111/jori.12437. Finding: An exogenous drop in analyst coverage raises risk-taking at property–casualty insurers, especially where managers have stronger risk-taking pay incentives.
- [Dual Ownership and Risk-Taking Incentives in Managerial Compensation](https://taochen.org/research/dual-ownership-risk-taking-rof-2023/) — Tao Chen, Li Zhang, Qifei Zhu. Review of Finance 27, 2023. DOI 10.1093/rof/rfad007. Finding: Firms with more “dual holders”, institutions that hold both their equity and their bonds, give CEOs less risk-inducing pay: fewer stock options and more inside debt.
- [Tariff uncertainty and firm innovation: Evidence from the U.S.–China Permanent Normal Trade Relation](https://taochen.org/research/tariff-uncertainty-firm-innovation-jef-2021/) — Tao Chen, Huasheng Gao, Yuxi Wang. Journal of Empirical Finance 62, 2021. DOI 10.1016/j.jempfin.2021.02.002. Finding: Lower tariff uncertainty on Chinese imports after Permanent Normal Trade Relations led affected U.S. firms to patent more, with more highly cited patents.
- [Marginal cost of risk-based capital and risk-taking](https://taochen.org/research/marginal-cost-risk-based-jbf-2019/) — Tao Chen, Jing Rong Goh, Shinichi Kamiya, Pingyi Lou. Journal of Banking & Finance 103, 2019. DOI 10.1016/j.jbankfin.2019.03.011. Finding: Insurers facing lower marginal risk-based capital costs buy riskier fixed-income securities, an unintended consequence of the capital formula’s diversification benefit.
- [Windfalls of emperors' sojourns: Stock market reactions to Chinese firms hosting high‐ranking government officials](https://taochen.org/research/windfalls-emperors-sojourns-stock-smj-2017/) — Douglas A. Schuler, Wei Shi, Robert E. Hoskisson, Tao Chen. Strategic Management Journal 38, 2017. DOI 10.1002/smj.2622. Finding: Investors react positively when Chinese firms host visits by the President or Premier, most of all for private firms and firms with weaker prior performance.
- [How does analysts' forecast quality relate to corporate investment efficiency?](https://taochen.org/research/analysts-forecast-quality-relate-jcf-2017/) — Tao Chen, Lingmin Xie, Yuanyuan Zhang. Journal of Corporate Finance 43, 2017. DOI 10.1016/j.jcorpfin.2016.12.010. Finding: Examines whether firms followed by analysts with higher-quality earnings forecasts invest more efficiently.
